newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate eases down on firm peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate eases down on firm peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates opened down 45 basis points at 19.55 percent in response to a strong open by the peso, traders said.
"The market is very quiet, under the infliuence of the peso, which in turn was a reflection of March trade balance figures, which in turn bolstered the market," an analyst said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were 0.65 of a centavo stronger in early trade at 7.8545/7.8575 per dollar.
Preliminary data released on Wednesday showed Mexico posted a trade balance of $565 million in March, compared with an average forecast of $324.29 million in a Reuters survey.
Dealers said market confidence in forthcoming inflation data had also allowed secondary interest rates to decline.
"Everyone expects inflation figures to show prices are still under control," the trader added.
A Reuters survey of Mexico City financial firms showed they forecast consumer prices would rise by an average of 0.64 percent during the first half of April.
Banco de Mexico is expected to release inflation data shortly before the close of trade.
Dealers said they felt secondary rates had reached floor levels.
"After the recent sustained slide, I think rates may have bottomed out; I don't think they should go any lower," a trader said.
Dealers also drew attention to the fact that the spread between government and bank rates had narrowed considerably.
"It is partly due to an overplacement of Cetes through repos and maybe because not so much bank paper has been issued," a money market analyst said.
Banco de Mexico recently changed its method of draining market liquidity, to assigning repos and direct Cetes sales, instead of deposit auctions.
Overnight rates on bank paper were meanwhile actually below government rates, having fallen 50 basis points to 19.50 percent.
Liquidity of 2.268 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
(( --Elena Vega, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9554))
"Rates fell so sharply on speculation, they're withholding paper in order to lower rates," a trader said.
Traders said three deals totalling 267.5 million pesos million pesos were settled at rates of 17.25 percent.
"Volume is very representative, a trader said.
Another dealer noted secondary market rates had also fallen after Banco de Mexico had participated in the market to drain liquidity.
The central bank assigned an overnight repo for 260 million pesos at the low rate of 18 percent as part of its intervention.
((--Elena Vega, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9554))
